title_en: Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Trial of Ship Collision Disputes

articles.content_en:
Article 1 For the purposes of these Provisions, "ship collision" means a ship collision as referred to in Article 165 of the Maritime Code, excluding collisions between inland river ships.
Damage accidents referred to in Article 170 of the Maritime Code shall be governed by these Provisions.

Article 2 In hearing cases of disputes over ship collisions, the compensation liability of the colliding ships shall be determined in accordance with the provisions of Chapter VIII of the Maritime Code.

Article 3 For tort disputes arising from a ship touching caused by a ship collision, the compensation liability of the colliding ships shall be determined in accordance with the provisions of Chapter VIII of the Maritime Code.
For tort disputes arising from a ship touching not caused by a ship collision, the compensation liability of the touching ship shall be determined in accordance with the provisions of the Civil Code, but this shall not affect the application of other provisions outside Chapter VIII of the Maritime Code.

Article 4 The compensation liability arising from a ship collision shall be borne by the ship owner. Where the colliding ship is under bareboat charter and has been registered according to law, the liability shall be borne by the bareboat charterer.

Article 5 Personal injury or death of persons on board caused by a ship collision shall fall within the scope of personal injury or death of third parties as provided in Article 169, paragraph 3 of the Maritime Code.

Article 6 Where the colliding ships are mutually at fault, causing loss of cargo on board, and the person entitled to the cargo on board brings an action for damages for breach of contract against the ship carrying the cargo, or brings an action for tort damages against one or both of the colliding ships, the People's Court shall accept the case according to law.

Article 7 Where the person entitled to cargo on board brings an action against the ship carrying the cargo for loss of the cargo caused by a ship collision, the carrying ship may, in accordance with Article 169, paragraph 2 of the Maritime Code, claim to bear compensation liability in proportion to the degree of fault.
The provisions of the preceding paragraph shall not affect the invocation by the carrier and the actual carrier of the provisions of Chapter IV of the Maritime Code concerning the carrier's grounds for defense and limitation of liability.

Article 8 Where the person entitled to cargo on board a colliding ship or a third party makes a claim for compensation against one or both of the colliding ships for loss of the cargo or other property, the colliding ship or ships shall provide evidence to prove the proportion of the degrees of fault. If the colliding ship or ships refuse to provide evidence without justifiable reasons, one colliding ship shall bear all the compensation liability, or both colliding ships shall bear joint and several compensation liability.
The evidence referred to in the preceding paragraph means legally effective judgments, rulings, mediation statements, and arbitration awards. Foreign judgments, rulings, mediation statements, and arbitration awards submitted by the colliding ships shall be examined in accordance with the procedures provided in Articles 282 and 283 of the Civil Procedure Law.

Article 9 For claims for compensation for the expenses of refloating, removing, demolishing, or rendering harmless a sunken, wrecked, stranded, or abandoned ship and cargo on board caused by a ship collision, the liable person shall not be entitled to the limitation of liability for maritime claims under the provisions of Chapter XI of the Maritime Code.

Article 10 When hearing a case of dispute over ship collision, evidence obtained by the People's Court through evidence preservation upon the application of a party or collected from the relevant authorities through investigation shall be presented after the parties have completed the presentation of evidence and issued a statement of completion of evidence presentation.

Article 11 After a ship collision accident occurs, the investigation materials on the facts of the collision obtained by the competent authority through investigation according to law and confirmed by the parties to the accident and the relevant personnel may be used as evidence for the People's Court to ascertain the facts of the case, unless there is contrary evidence sufficient to overturn them.
